subject: Performance SLO + Private VPC qualification — network path & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLO + Private VPC qualification — network path & next steps

Hi Alice / Raj,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and helpful context on Acme Analytics' performance targets for the private deployment. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key SLOs and the network/connectivity items we need to qualify before we scope the PoC. Please confirm or correct anything below: 

Summary of SLOs/requirements you mentioned:
- P95 latency target for end-to-end token response: <= 120ms; P99 target: <= 250ms (streaming partial tokens acceptable).
- Target throughput: sustained ~200 requests/sec for bulk inference (non-streaming), bursts to 400rps tolerated for 2-5min windows.
- Concurrent inference sessions: ~20 concurrent streaming sessions, each with average 512 tokens context.
- Streaming: must support low-latency token streaming to the client (websocket or HTTP chunked).
- Internal app-to-endpoint latency budget: <30ms preferred; if >50ms we will need closer placement or additional routing.

Network & private deployment notes you shared:
- You prefer VPC Peering to the Redwood Private control plane and an on-prem worker pool that can reach our inference nodes via a customer-managed VPN or direct peering.
- Egress constraints: only specific egress IPs allowed; traffic must be NAT'd through your perimeter.
- Bastion host is available in us-west-2 for test traffic; no direct internet egress from internal services.

Immediate items we need from Acme to validate feasibility for the PoC:
1) Network diagram (attached: acme-network-diagram.png) with CIDRs, NAT/egress points, and bastion details.
2) VPN endpoints and retained firewall rules (attach existing VPN config / IP allowlist).
3) A small sample of internal latency measurements (traceroute/iperf results) from app->bastion and bastion->inference candidate IPs (if available).
4) Confirmation on whether WebSocket streaming ports are allowed through perimeter.

Proposed next steps / PoC outline (we can finalize after we get the items above):
- Step 0: Red team and Acme network team run a quick traceroute + iperf to a Redwood test endpoint from your bastion.
- Step 1: Short PoC (2 weeks): deploy a small Redwood Private worker pool in your VPC (or peered subnet) and run baseline latency/throughput tests at your scale.
- Step 2: Ramp up to concurrency goals and validate streaming behavior + tail latency with your representative traffic.

Can you send the artifacts above (2-3 items in bold) and confirm a 30-45 minute window early next week for the first network test? I’ve copied our infra lead David Kim to help with the test plan and any packet captures we might need.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme-network-diagram.png

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Security <secops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO + Private VPC qualification — network path & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the high-level SLOs are correct (we're intentionally conservative on P99 for now). I attached the items you asked for: vpn-endpoints.txt (contains our current VPN endpoints and allowed peer IPs) and internal-latency.csv (sample traceroute/latency metrics from our app to the bastion).

Quick answers inline: \- WebSocket streaming: allowed through perimeter on ports 443 and 8443; custom ports will require additional change window.
- Egress: all outbound to 52.66.0.0/16 is allowed through our NAT; anything outside that needs a request.
- Bastion: us-west-2b, reachable via SSH via our SSM jumpbox; we can run iperf and traceroute on request.

We can do the first network test Monday 2026-07-06 at 10:00 PT. Raj (cc'd) is our infrastructure lead and can coordinate SSH access to the bastion. Let me know the Redwood endpoint IP to test against and any specific iperf options/ports.

Thanks,
Alice
Senior SRE, Acme Analytics
alice.nguyen@acme-analytics.com

Attachments: vpn-endpoints.txt, internal-latency.csv

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO + Private VPC qualification — network path & next steps

Awesome, thanks Alice — that's very helpful.

Quick clarifications before the test Monday: \- Can you confirm whether the bastion is allowed to initiate outbound TCP connections on 443/8443 to the Redwood test IPs? If outbound to those CIDRs is blocked, we'll need the jumpbox to proxy the tests.
- For iperf, we'll test TCP with -P 10 parallel streams for a 30s run and UDP at 64kb packet size for 30s to capture jitter. Will that be OK from your side?
- Do you have any packet sampling that we can use (tops-1s) to look at per-packet latency during a streaming session?

I added David and Rishi from our infra/solutions teams to coordinate. David — can you share the temporary test endpoint(s) and a short PoC test plan doc? I've also uploaded a short draft PoC test plan here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmeNetDiag (link contains test steps + expected metrics).

If Monday 10:00 PT works, I'll send a calendar invite for the 30-minute window and set up a short checklist for the run (traceroute, iperf TCP/UDP, sample streaming session).

-Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme PoC network test — prep + responsibilities

David / Rishi — quick internal note and proposed runbook for Monday's test (2026-07-06 10:00 PT). Keeping it short: 

Goal: Validate whether Acme's private path (bastion->peered subnet) can meet the internal latency budget (<30ms app->endpoint) and whether streaming tail latency stays within P99 <= 250ms at expected concurrency.

Proposed test steps:
1) Provide customer with temporary Redwood test IP(s) (David) — include both TCP (443) and a websocket test port (8443).
2) Customer runs: traceroute -> capture RTTs; iperf TCP -P 10, 30s; iperf UDP 30s at 64kb; and a streaming session using our sample client (we'll provide script).
3) Collect packet captures on the bastion for one streaming session (30s) — request pcap and tops-1s latencies.
4) Run load: simulate 20 concurrent streaming sessions (representative payload) and measure P50/P95/P99 for token arrival. We'll do incremental ramps: 5 -> 10 -> 20 concurrent.
5) If all good, enable a small private worker pool in their peered subnet and run the same tests end-to-end.

Notes / requirements: \- Be prepared to offer a short term NAT'ed egress IP if their NAT denies our test IPs; we may need a scheduled change window.
- If outbound from bastion is restricted, we can run reverse tests (our side initiate to their bastion) but that requires SSH proxying.

Action items:
- David: provision test endpoints and share IPs + cert fingerprints by EOD Friday (2026-07-03).
- Rishi: prepare the streaming client script and a short PoC checklist doc (PoC-test-plan.docx) with exact iperf flags, websocket sample payload, and expected metric collection fields.
- Marissa: coordinate invite and communicate checklist to Acme.

I'll attach the draft PoC plan once Rishi provides it and loop in account exec for any contractual notes. This looks like a solid mid-market PoC; if tests pass we can scope Dedicated/Private pricing for ACME-2026-42.

-Marissa
